newsitem.title: USA: New World intends to buy coffee company.
newsitem.headline: New World intends to buy coffee company.

text.p: New World Coffee Inc said Wednesday it has signed a letter of intent to acquire Willoughby's Coffee & Tea.
Willoughby's Coffee & Tea, a private specialty coffee roaster and retailer, is based in New Haven, Conn.
It owns and operates a roasting facility and five stores in central Connecticut. A sixth store is scheduled to open next month in New Haven.
The stores will initially retain the Willoughby's name but eventually will take on the New World Coffee name, a spokesman said.
Through an exclusive contract, Willoughby's has been the coffee purchaser and roaster for New World since it was founded in 1984.
New World President and Chief Executive Ramin Kamfar said acquiring Willoughby's will allow it to expand its wholesale and mail-order business, an area in which Willoughby's has a strong base.
Barry Levine and Bob Williams, the founders of Willoughby's, are to become key executive officers in charge of coffee for New World. Their new positions were not disclosed.
